dedomenon.definition: Perfect passive participle of δίδωμι ('to give'): a geometric object or attribute whose equal, ratio, species, or position is either posited in the hypothesis or constructively procurable from the hypotheses.

tetagmenon.definition: In Apollonius and Marinus (pp. 234–236), that which always preserves one and the same determination in nature without varying—such as the straight line through two fixed points or the circle through three.

atakton.definition: Contrary of τεταγμένον in Marinus (p. 236): a configuration admitting infinitely many undetermined realizations (ἀπειραχῶς), such as a circle through only two points or an unspecified scalene triangle.

gnorimon.definition: In Diodorus and Marinus (pp. 234, 238–240), that which has come into cognitive grasp relative to us (πρὸς ἡμᾶς), serving as the genus in Marinus's composite definition of δεδομένον as γνώριμον ἅμα καὶ πόριμον.

porimon.definition: In Euclid (Defs. 1–2, πορίσασθαι) and Marinus (pp. 240, 250), that which we have the actual constructive means to produce or exhibit from the elementary postulates; distinguished from ποριστόν (potentially solvable).

aporon.definition: Contrary of πόριμον in Marinus (p. 240): a problem or magnitude whose constructive method has not yet been mastered (exemplified for the ancients by the quadrature of the circle).

rheton.definition: In Ptolemy and Marinus (pp. 234, 240–242), a magnitude expressible by a known number relative to a conventional unit measure (μέτρον); strictly narrower than δεδομένον, since √2 is given (Data 43/52) yet ἄλογον.

alogon.definition: In Elements Book X and Marinus (pp. 240–244), an incommensurable magnitude such as the diagonal of a unit square or a binomial (ἐκ δύο ὀνομάτων), which is nonetheless fully δεδομένον (procurable and determinate).

megethei.definition: Data Def. 1: spaces, lines, and angles are given in magnitude when we can construct equals to them (equivalence up to congruence / measure).

logo.definition: Data Def. 2: a ratio A : B is given when we can procure an identical ratio C : D between constructible given magnitudes.

eidei.definition: Data Def. 3: rectilinear figures are given in species when every interior angle is given in magnitude and all ratios of their sides to one another are given (invariance under Euclidean similarity).

thesei.definition: Data Def. 4: points, lines, and angles are given in position when they always occupy the same fixed place in the planar reference frame (and, per Simson's refinement, are exhibited or constructible).

analyomenos-topos.definition: In Pappus (Synagoge VII) and Marinus (p. 252), the curated corpus of advanced Greek treatises—opening with Euclid's Data—designed to equip the geometer with the power of analytical problem-solving.

analysis.definition: Method of discovery assuming the sought object as realized and tracing deductive consequences via the Data until every component is proved 'given' from the problem's hypotheses.

synthesis.definition: Constructive reversal of a valid analysis: executing the elementary constructions corresponding to each Data step in forward order and proving that the resulting figure satisfies the problem.

diorismos.definition: Necessary Inequality or constructibility condition governing whether a problem admits 0, 1, or 2 solutions (e.g., Data 31 circle-line distance, Data 44 SSA acute/obtuse split, Data 58 discriminant).

parabole.definition: Applying a given area S along a given segment a in a given angle without excess or defect (Elements I.44, Data 57), solving the linear equation a · x · sin θ = S.

elleipsis.definition: Applying a given area S to a given segment a falling short by a parallelogram of given species (Elements VI.28, Data 58, Data 85), solving the quadratic equation x(a − c·x) = S.

hyperbole.definition: Applying a given area S to a given segment a exceeding by a parallelogram of given species (Elements VI.29, Data 59, Data 84), solving the quadratic equation x(a + c·x) = S (including the golden section).

gnomon.definition: Any of the two complements together with one of the parallelograms about the diameter of a parallelogram (Elements II.def.2); adding or subtracting a gnomon preserves species (Data 60).

dynamis.definition: The area of the square on a straight line (τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς εὐθείας τετράγωνον); magnitudes 'greater in square' (δυνάμει μείζων) govern the cosine-law and biquadratic propositions Data 64–67 and 86.

dothenti-meizon-e-en-logo.translation: greater by a given magnitude than in ratio
dothenti-meizon-e-en-logo.definition: Data Def. 11: Euclid's compact idiom for the affine-linear relation (A − D) : B = k (i.e., A = k·B + D with given offset D and given slope k), systematically closed under composition and elimination in Data 10–21.

kategmene.definition: Bracketed Data Def. 13 (from conic/locus terminology): a straight line drawn from a given point onto a straight line given in position in a given angle (cf. Data 30).

anegmene.definition: Bracketed Data Def. 14: a straight line erected from a given point upon a straight line given in position at a given angle (cf. Data 29).

para-thesei.translation: parallel to a line given in position
para-thesei.definition: Bracketed Data Def. 15: a straight line drawn through a given point parallel to a straight line given in position (cf. Data 28).
